summary: Late close-frame delivered during pooled WS connection reuse causes partial final chunk and dangling attachment metadata
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent truncated/partial final output when using WebSocket streaming behind connection pooling and TLS 0-RTT fallback. In the failing sessions a WS connection close frame appears to arrive after a pooled socket is returned to the pool; the client observes a short extra fragment containing attachment metadata (e.g. 'attachments':[{}]) and a truncated last sentence or emoji. Impact: InkboxAI (enterprise) has production customers seeing ~1-3% of streamed responses end with partial JSON envelope or dangling attachment field; downstream parsers fail and the UX shows 'incomplete result'. Environment: prod, us-east-1, mostly observed with long-running streaming sessions (>30s) and intermittent TLS fallback to 0-RTT when client resumes on flaky mobile networks. Steps to reproduce (representative): 1) Start a streaming WebSocket generation request using SDK JS with keepAlive: true and multiplexing disabled. 2) Simulate mobile network churn: drop network briefly and reconnect using TLS 0-RTT. 3) Allow connection pool to reuse the socket for a new session within ~200ms window. 4) Observe client-side event stream: a close frame (1006/abrupt) or late control frame arrives interleaved with final delta messages. Observed behavior: - Client receives an extra small text frame containing metadata-only JSON like '{"attachments":[{}],"_partial":true}' after what appears to be the terminal choice. - The final natural-language sentence is cut mid-word and no terminal 'done' marker is present in the application envelope. - Chrome-based clients show a WebSocket close code 1006 in the timeline; server logs show normal end-of-stream but a late FIN/close on pooled connection. Expected behavior: - Close frames and any control frames should be sequenced so that final application payloads are delivered atomically; clients should not receive metadata-only fragments without a proper terminal application marker. Additional context/attachments: - Customer provided SDK traces and HAR of WS lifecycle. - Slack thread: #support /thread/CF7AB12 - Customer asserts this started after recent edge-pool optimization rollout.
steps_to_reproduce: Use SDK JS v3.4.1 with streaming WebSocket enabled and keepAlive=true
Open a long streaming generation (>30s) that emits structured metadata attachments in the final choice
Simulate a network drop and reconnect using a client that supports TLS 0-RTT (mobile suspend/resume)
Allow the connection pool to hand the socket back to the pool and then immediately reuse it for a new session
Observe the client-side WS event order and final JSON assembly

comments: Ava Martinez (Support): Received initial report from InkboxAI. They included SDK logs and a short HAR trace. Reproduces against prod us-east. Marking P1 and escalating to runtime team.

Samir Patel (SRE): I can reproduce locally by running a TLS 0-RTT reconnection script + immediate pool reuse. Looks like pool GC returns socket before server-side close handshake completes. Captured tcpdump shows late FIN after WS delta frames.

Elena K (Runtime): Hypothesis: edge connection-pool fast-reuse optimization returns socket to pool while server control frames still buffered on underlying TCP. If the pool hands socket to a new logical session, client sees a mixed fragment. Adding a 200ms grace on pool return reduces rate in local testing.

Ava Martinez (Support): Shared temporary workaround to customer: set sdk.keepAliveTimeout to 300ms and upgrade to SDK JS 3.4.2-beta that includes client-side reassembly resilience. Customer accepted workaround and will monitor.
Samir Patel (SRE): Created PR to add graceful drain window (200ms) on pool return: GH PR #2287. Running canary in us-east on a subset of edge nodes.
InkboxAI (customer, support contact Marco Li): Verified workaround reduces occurrences in our staging traffic. Will validate in production over next 48 hours.
investigation_notes: Reproducible with TLS 0-RTT path + pool reuse under high churn in lab (scripted mobile disconnects)
tcpdump shows server emits FIN/close after last application frame; edge proxy sometimes coalesces the control frame into a subsequent socket handed to new session
Edge pool change deployed last week (edge-pool: fast-return=true) corresponds with first reports from customer
Hypothesis: race between pool return (socket moved to idle set) and arrival of server close frame from origin; new session reads trailing control frame as part of application stream
Short-term mitigation verified: client-side reassembly (ignore metadata-only fragment if terminal marker seen) reduces failures by ~95% in customer tests
Long-term fix: implement server/edge drain window (200-500ms) before making pooled socket reusable and add strict control-frame separation at proxy layer
resolution: Workaround provided: InkboxAI updated to SDK JS 3.4.2-beta which applies client-side tolerant reassembly for trailing metadata and set keepAliveTimeout=300ms. Engineering deployed edge drain-window canary (PR #2287) to us-east on 10% of nodes which reduced incident rate from ~2.5% to 0.1% in canary. Next steps: roll out drain window globally, add proxy invariant to reject control frames on new logical sessions, and add automated test for pooled-socket late control frames. Customer to confirm stability after 48h; ticket will be updated and closed on confirmation.
